# Review context, round 2: route protected-path changes through pull requests

Range for this round: 56f3b8b4..91e82480, one follow-up commit on top of the reviewed commit
`docs: route protected-path changes through pull requests`. Read the whole "Protected paths" bullet in
`.agents/skills/project-delivery/references/workflow.md` at HEAD, not only the changed lines.

Settled round-1 findings. Treat each as fixed in this range; reject a claim that the fix is wrong only with
evidence from the files.

- The maintainer-approval exception let an agent push a protected change, because the agent writes the
  commit body that quotes the approval (one P1 and one P2 from two reviewers). Fixed: the exception is
  removed. Protected paths go through a pull request, and only the maintainer pushes them directly.
- The Named branch bullet forbids the separate branch a pull request needs (P2). Fixed: the protected-path
  bullet authorizes that branch and the pull request.
- The bullet restated the integrity job's pull-request-only trigger (P3). Fixed: the bullet no longer states
  it; the rule rests on code-owner review.

Attack surfaces for this round. Read each file named.

1. Completeness of the bypass closure. With the exception gone, list every route by which an agent could
   land a change to a protected path without a pull request. Check `.agents/skills/project-delivery/SKILL.md`
   ("Authority And Stops" and the delivery steps), `.agents/skills/project-delivery/references/workflow.md`
   (every delivery bullet), and `design/issue-automation.md` (the unattended runner's human-merge list and
   its auto-merge rule). Report any route that remains open.
2. Consistency of protected lists. The bullet points at the Protected infrastructure list in
   `verification/verification-integrity.md`. Compare that list with the runner's human-merge list in
   `design/issue-automation.md`. Report any protected path the runner could merge unattended.
3. Link and anchor. Confirm that `../../../../verification/verification-integrity.md#protected-infrastructure`
   resolves from `.agents/skills/project-delivery/references/`.
4. Commit body. Each commit must list the MUST and MUST NOT lines it adds or changes. Check that the
   follow-up commit does so, and that its assurance reason fits `.agents/skills/project-delivery/references/assurance.md`.
5. Writing. The bullet should state the rule once, front-load its trigger, avoid restating facts that
   another document owns, and avoid line numbers and commit hashes.

For each finding, give the file, the heading or rule text, a severity (blocking, high, medium, or low), the
evidence, and the smallest fix. A protected-path gap that lies outside this bullet is still a finding; say
whether this change should fix it or a separate change should. If there are no findings, say so.
Do not edit files.

summary: The follow-up commit removes the approval exception, authorizes the separate branch and pull request, and drops the integrity-job restatement; the link and anchor resolve, and the commit lists its MUST/MUST NOT with a skip reason that fits assurance.md. Two protected-path gaps remain outside the bullet: the unattended runner's human-merge list (doc and code) omits verification/verification-integrity.md, which is both a Protected infrastructure path and the list the new bullet routes on, so the runner can auto-merge a rewrite of it; and the delivery rule's own file (.agents/skills/project-delivery/) is not a protected path, so an agent can still remove the rule by direct push before pushing a protected change. The second is a separate-change defense-in-depth item.

findings.title: Runner's human-merge list omits the protected verification contract
findings.trigger: A maintainer authorizes an issue with agent/ready whose fix modifies verification/verification-integrity.md, for example narrowing the Protected infrastructure list or adding an exception. The runner's diff-policy gate classifies the change as neither forbidden nor human-merge, pushes auto/issue-*, opens a PR, and land() squash-merges it without a human.
findings.consequence: The protected-path contract that the new delivery bullet uses as its trigger can be rewritten unattended, shrinking the set of paths routed through pull requests and bypassing the code-owner review the bullet promises; the runner merges its own PR, so no code-owner review gates that landing.
findings.evidence: verification/verification-integrity.md:57 lists this contract as Protected infrastructure; design/issue-automation.md:164-167 and scripts/issue_agent/policy.py:22-25 omit verification/ from the human-merge prefixes/files; scripts/issue_agent/policy.py:124-132 (classify_paths) returns no human path for a modification of it; scripts/issue_agent/landing.py:141-181 (human_reasons/land/merge) auto-merges when human_paths is empty; .agents/skills/project-delivery/references/workflow.md:94-99 routes protected paths on that same list.
findings.suggestedFix: Add verification/verification-integrity.md (or verification/) to the runner's human-merge list in design/issue-automation.md section 6 and to HUMAN_PREFIXES/HUMAN_FILES in scripts/issue_agent/policy.py, ideally deriving the runner's list from the Protected infrastructure list so the two cannot drift; land that as a protected-path change through a pull request.

findings.title: The rule's own file is not a protected path
findings.trigger: An agent directly pushes a commit that deletes or narrows the Protected paths bullet in workflow.md (or the SKILL.md delivery steps), then directly pushes the protected change. The first push touches no path in the Protected infrastructure list, so the new rule does not apply to it.
findings.consequence: The bypass the change claims to close stays open: the trigger for the protected-path rule is defined by a file an agent can rewrite without a pull request, so the rule is voluntary for the agent it constrains.
findings.evidence: verification/verification-integrity.md:54-57 and .github/CODEOWNERS:1-6 omit .agents/; design/issue-automation.md:165-167 treats .agents/skills/project-delivery/ as human-merge-required precisely because an agent must not rewrite its own instructions unattended, but the Protected infrastructure list the new bullet points at does not.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate change: add .agents/skills/project-delivery/ (at least the delivery references) to the Protected infrastructure list in verification/verification-integrity.md and to .github/CODEOWNERS, so editing the rule requires the same pull-request route; until then the bullet should not be read as closing every route.
